newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police arrest three in 1969 bomb probe.
newsitem.headline: Italian police arrest three in 1969 bomb probe.

text.p: Italian anti-terrorist police arrested three people on Saturday in connection with the 1969 bombing of a Milan bank in which 16 people were killed and more than 80 injured, news agencies said.
The arrests were also connected with investigations into an attack on Milan police offices in 1973 in which four people died and 46 were hurt.
Those held were linked to a regional neo-fascist group, ANSA news agency said.
The bombing of Banca Nazionale dell'Agricoltura in Milan's Piazza Fontana on December 12, 1969, marked the start of over a decade of terrorist attacks in Italy.
Hundreds of people died in the so-called "years of lead" between 1969 and 1984, variously blamed on neo-fascists, the extreme left and rogue members of the Italian secret services.
